name: Chambéry Tarot
description: Early 20th century French Tarot from Chambéry, Savoy. Three to five players; with four or five, partnerships form by Solo bid or dealer calling a King. Objective: win the majority of 68 card points (52 from counting cards plus 15 tricks and the discard). Uses 78-card French Tarot; trumps rank 21 down to 1; Fool may be shown once and added to team's tricks.

history.origins: Rules by the Club des Taroteurs in the Grand Café Emile Coudurier in Chambéry, capital of French Savoy, accompanying the 1902 Tarot français des fleurs (French Flower Tarot) by Fossorier, Amar & Cie. Savoy belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia until 1860; rules resemble Piedmont and Nice Tarot more than modern French Tarot.
timeline: 1902: Tarot français des fleurs pack and Chambéry rules published.
Present: Playable with any 78-card French Tarot; Dussere reprint available.
history.cultural: Played in Chambéry cafés; linked to Savoyard and Piedmontese Tarot traditions.
history.evolution: Four- and three-player variants and a shortened 62-card pack (tarot simplifié) extend the same scoring and bidding ideas.

setup.players: Three to five; five preferred. With four or five, partnerships (Solo or called partner). With three, each plays for themselves.
setup.deck: A French-suited Tarot pack of 78 cards: 22 trumps (tarots) ranking 21 down to 1, the Fool (Fou), and 56 suit cards in four suits (King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, then Ace and numerals 10–2). The standard game uses the full pack; a shortened 62-card version (tarot simplifié) exists for three or four players.
setup.dealing: Deal and play anticlockwise. Dealer rotates right after each hand. Five players: dealer gives packets of 5 three times around so each non-dealer gets 15 cards; dealer takes last 3 (18 total) then discards 3 face down. Dealer may not discard Kings, 21, or Fou; other tarots only if dealer would have no tarots left. Four players: each gets 19 cards (e.g. 5,5,5,4); dealer gets 6 last and discards 2. Three players: each gets 25 in five packets of 5; dealer gets 3 extra (28) and discards 3.
setup.equipment: 78-card French Tarot pack; chips (50 points per player) optional for scoring.

rules.objective: Win the majority of card points. In five-player: 68 points total (52 counting cards, 15 tricks, 1 for discard); tie at 34. Team with fewer than 34 pays the difference to the winners; payment may be doubled or quadrupled for Solo or low score.
rules.gameplay: Bidding: first hand (right of dealer) may bid a Solo (2-Card, 1-Card, or Hand Solo) or pass; later player may bid a Solo with fewer cards to supersede. If no Solo, dealer calls a King (or Queen if dealer holds all Kings) for partner. Play: player to dealer's right leads; must follow suit, else play a tarot; if neither possible, any card. No obligation to overtake. Highest tarot wins the trick, else highest of led suit. Fool may be shown once and added to own team's tricks; it never wins a trick.
keyRules: Must follow suit if able; if unable, must play a tarot; if neither, any card. No obligation to overtake.
Trumps (tarots) rank 21 down to 1. Fool is not a tarot for following; may be played once as excuse to own team's tricks.
Dealer may not discard Kings, 21, or Fou. Soloist may demand one or two cards (not Fou) from opponents in exchange for unwanted cards.
Card points: Fou, 21, 1 = 4 each; Kings 4; Queens 3; Cavaliers 2; Jacks 1; each trick and the discard count 1 extra.

strategy.basic: Count trumps and Kings; avoid discarding counting cards as dealer when possible. In Solo, demand high trumps or Kings.
strategy.intermediate: Time when to play the Fool so it goes to a trick your side wins. Save high trumps for key tricks.
strategy.advanced: In call games, infer partner from who supports your leads. In Solo, manage the exchange to strengthen your long suits.
tips: Dealer cannot discard Kings, 21, or Fou; plan your discard accordingly.
Fool never wins a trick but can be shown once to your team's pile.

variations.name: Four-Player Chambéry
variations.description: Each player receives 19 cards (e.g. 5,5,5,4); dealer gets 6 last and discards 2. 72 card points total; tie at 36. Play with Solo/call or fixed partnerships (partners opposite).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal and point totals differ from five-player; engine constants could override dealPattern and point totals if needed.

variations.name: Three-Player Chambéry
variations.description: Each receives 25 cards in five packets of 5; dealer gets 3 extra (28) and discards 3. No partnerships, no Solo. 78 card points; players under 26 pay the difference (doubled if under 13).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal size and scoring differ; no partnerships or Solo; engine overrides could be added for dealPattern and scoring.

variations.name: Tarot simplifié (shortened pack)
variations.description: Remove 2, 3, 4, 5 from each suit (62 cards). Three or four players; different deal and scoring; see source for details.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Shortened pack and different deal; full overrides would require deck and deal changes; see source for details.

scoring.description: 68 card points in five-player (52 counting cards, 15 tricks, 1 discard); tie at 34. Team with fewer than 34 pays the difference; doubled if losers have fewer than 17, doubled for 1-Card Solo, quadrupled for Hand Solo (max 8× for Hand Solo with losers under 17).
scoring.winCondition: Team or player with more than half of the card points wins; tie at half. Losers pay the difference with possible multipliers (Solo, low score).

synthesis.shortDescription: Early 20th century French Tarot from Chambéry, Savoy. Three to five players; Solo or call a King; 68 card points, must follow suit, trumps 21–1, Fool may be shown once.
